verses.text: Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
After fasting forty days and forty nights, He was hungry.
The tempter came to Him and said, "If You are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread."
But Jesus answered, "It is written: 'Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.'"
Then the devil took Him to the holy city and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple.

"If You are the Son of God," he said, "throw Yourself down. For it is written: 'He will command His angels concerning You, and they will lift You up in their hands, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.'"
Jesus replied, "It is also written: 'Do not put the Lord your God to the test.'"
Again, the devil took Him to a very high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
"All this I will give You," he said, "if You will fall down and worship me."
"Away from Me, Satan!" Jesus told him. "For it is written: 'Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.'"
Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him.
When Jesus heard that John had been imprisoned, He withdrew to Galilee.
Leaving Nazareth, He went and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,
to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah:
"Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles—
the people living in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned."
From that time on Jesus began to preach, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near."
As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
"Come, follow Me," Jesus said, "and I will make you fishers of men."
And at once they left their nets and followed Him.
Going on from there, He saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets. Jesus called them,
and immediately they left the boat and their father and followed Him.
Jesus went throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.

News about Him spread all over Syria, and people brought to Him all who were ill with various diseases, those suffering acute pain, the demon-possessed, those having seizures, and the paralyzed, and He healed them.
Large crowds followed Him, having come from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan.

context.author: Matthew, writing to a Jewish audience
context.genre: Narrative — temptation account followed by the launch of Jesus' public ministry.
context.audience: Jewish-Christian readers who would recognize Jesus quoting Deuteronomy three times, succeeding where Israel itself had failed during its own forty years of wilderness testing.
context.setting: The rugged Judean desert west of the Dead Sea, then a deliberate move north to Capernaum — a fishing town on the Sea of Galilee sitting on the Via Maris, a major trade highway linking Egypt and Damascus.
context.custom: Forty days of fasting deliberately parallels Israel's forty years in the wilderness and Moses' forty-day fast on Sinai — where Israel failed repeatedly, Jesus stands firm.
context.timelineImmediate: Immediately after His baptism in chapter 3 — this marks the true beginning of Jesus' public ministry, roughly three years before the crucifixion.
context.timelineBible: This is the launch point of everything that follows in the Gospels — every teaching, healing, and confrontation in the rest of Matthew flows out of this chapter's opening act of public ministry.

translation.meaning: Can mean either "tempted" or "tested" — the same event functions as both an attack and a proof of character.
The same call John used in chapter 3 — Jesus now takes up and embodies the message Himself.
A deliberate play on the disciples' actual trade — turning a fishing metaphor into a calling.

gospelParallels.note: Mark's much shorter account of the same wilderness temptation.
Luke records the same three temptations in a different order.

otBackground.note: "Man does not live on bread alone" — Jesus' first response to the devil, quoted directly.
"Do not put the Lord your God to the test" — Jesus' second response.
The prophecy of light dawning on Galilee, quoted as fulfilled in v.15-16.
